name: Attention Context & Influence Channels
description: Understanding how much attention and time a user has in a given interaction context, and selecting the right influence mechanism accordingly. Two primary contexts: Fleeting Attention (the user is momentarily present — use simple, urgent, bite-sized interventions) and Many Chances to Influence (the user has recurring engagement — use rich, relationship-building, behavior-forming mechanics).

subskills.name: Fleeting Attention — Call to Action (CTA)
subskills.description: Designing high-impact calls to action for contexts where user attention is momentary. Covers CTA copywriting (action verb + benefit), visual prominence (contrast, size, whitespace), placement (above the fold, end of content), A/B testing CTAs, and micro-copy that reduces friction and anxiety at the point of action.

subskills.name: Fleeting Attention — Status Reports
subskills.description: Delivering concise, scannable status updates that inform the user about system state, progress, or next actions without requiring sustained attention. Covers dashboard widgets, notification badges, status indicators, email digests, and push notification summaries designed for scanning rather than reading.

subskills.name: Fleeting Attention — How-to Tips & Reminders
subskills.description: Short, contextually triggered micro-learning moments delivered at the point of relevance. Includes tooltips, empty state guidance, coachmarks, contextual reminders (scheduled or event-triggered), and in-app guidance that surfaces exactly when the user needs it without being disruptive.

subskills.name: Many Chances — Gamification
subskills.description: Applying game mechanics to non-game contexts to drive sustained engagement. Covers points, badges, leaderboards (PBL framework), levels, challenges, quests, and unlockable content. Distinguishes between intrinsic motivation mechanics (mastery, purpose) and extrinsic mechanics (rewards, competition), and warns against over-reliance on extrinsic rewards that undermine intrinsic motivation.

subskills.name: Many Chances — Planners & Goal Trackers
subskills.description: Designing planning and goal-setting interfaces that sustain long-term behavior change. Covers goal-setting frameworks (SMART goals, OKR alignment), calendar-based planning UIs, habit trackers, streaks, weekly review flows, and retrospective prompts that keep users accountable over extended periods.

subskills.name: Many Chances — Tutorials & Progressive Onboarding
subskills.description: Multi-session learning experiences that build user competence over time. Covers interactive tutorials, product tours, skill progression paths, contextual onboarding sequences that adapt to user behavior, and post-onboarding re-engagement flows that address churn risk at the Day 3, Day 7, and Day 30 milestones.

subskills.name: Many Chances — Social Sharing
subskills.description: Designing social proof and sharing mechanics that leverage the social influence vector over repeated interactions. Covers shareable achievement cards, social progress comparisons, peer leaderboards, referral mechanics, and community-building features that create network effects and peer accountability.

junior.description: Designs high-quality CTAs, contextual tooltips, and scannable status indicators for low-attention contexts.

mid.description: Designs gamified engagement loops, goal tracker UIs, and multi-session onboarding flows for sustained behavioral engagement.
